correctness.rationale: Direct group multiplication yields necessary and sufficient involution and commutator equations. For rank-d X, symmetric zero-diagonal XY is an alternating form on the d-space quotient, giving q^{d(d-1)/2} products and q^{r(b-d)} Y-lifts. Counting rank-d X by Gaussian subspaces and surjections gives every summand; central coordinates are arbitrary. Normalization at fixed q,r proves the stated limit. Independent GF2/GF4 exhaustive checks passed 14 cases.
